By performing a systematic, multi-rapidity blast-wave analysis of experimental invariant yields, we extract the continuous rapidity density profile $\rho_{\mathrm{net}}(y)$ and the transverse momentum broadening profile $\langle p_T^2 \rangle_{\mathrm{net}}(y)$. Utilizing a stochastic diffusion framework governed by relativistic Fokker-Planck dynamics, we analytically derive the longitudinal friction coefficient $\alpha_{\mathrm{bw}}$, the rapidity diffusion coefficient $D_y$, the longitudinal relaxation time $\tau_{\mathrm{relax}}$, and the associated longitudinal Reynolds number $\mathrm{Re}_L$. Our extracted central stopping fractions demonstrate qualitative consistency with the previous published two source thermal calculations. Crucially, the excitation function of $\mathrm{Re}_L$ reveals a drop by a factor of $\sim 163$, from $\mathrm{Re}_L \approx 4.88$ at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.70\text{ GeV}$ to $\mathrm{Re}_L \approx 0.03$ at $62.4\text{ GeV}$. This provides a clear macroscopic baseline for the crossover from inertial, advection-dominated baryon stopping to thermal, diffusion-dominated nuclear transparency, establishing a solid data-driven baseline for the topological baryon junction dynamics and high-$\mu_B$ matter anticipated at upcoming facilities, including FAIR, NICA, and the CEE.

papers.title: Radio and high-energy variable emission from a multi-wavelength follow-up of the infant planet-hosting star V1298 Tau
papers.abstract: V1298 Tau is a very young and magnetically active K1V star which hosts a benchmark multi-planetary system to study planet formation and evolutionary history at the earliest stages. Between 2025 and 2026, we conducted a campaign to monitor the variability of V1298 Tau in radio (band C), X-ray, and NUV bands, with the support of publicly available contemporary optical light curve, and to investigate multi-band correlations to link the emission with stellar activity. Radio observations were carried out with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (JVLA) in band C (4.5--6.5 GHz). X-ray and NUV observations were carried out with the Swift satellite over 20 days, ending one month before the begin of the radio campaign. We analysed the temporal variability of peak (integrated) fluxes in the C-band and of X-ray (NUV) luminosities on various timescales, comparing it with the variability observed in the high-cadence optical light curve collected by the ASAS-SN survey. We observed both radio and high-energy time variable emission. JVLA detected emission in 90\% of the visits, switching between high ($\geq$0.1 mJy/beam) and low flux states in matter of days or hours. The fluxes show moderate correlation with the optical light curve, suggesting modulation with the stellar rotation period. Except for one visit, dynamic spectral analysis does not reveal short-term (minutes) variability, nor is there any evidence of circularly polarised emissions. Overall, the radio observations can be explained as gyrosynchrotron and/or cyclotron emission from the corona, and linked to stellar magnetic activity. At high-energy, we detected significant variability in X-ray luminosity (within the range ~1.2--2.5x10$^{+30}$ erg/s), the decay phase of a stellar flare, and evidence of correlation with the optical flux. Our data confirm that V1298\,Tau follows the near-linear G\"udel-Benz relation.

papers.title: An end-to-end function for the photograph of a Schwarzschild black hole
papers.abstract: We show that the photograph of a Schwarzschild black hole can be written in closed form. The image plane is embedded as a plane tangent to a sphere centred on the black hole, and the map between a point source and its image point, which we call the photograph function, is treated as the analytic object. Explicit expressions are obtained for sources on the celestial sphere at infinity and for sources in the equatorial plane, without solving for the intermediate null geodesics. The construction is exact, and it makes the multivalued branch structure, the relation to the photon sphere and to the shadow boundary, and the self-similar higher-order images directly readable.

papers.title: Searches for coincident Gravitational Waves and High-Energy Neutrinos from the KM3NeT and ANTARES telescopes during O3
papers.abstract: Various models predict that gravitational-wave sources produce high-energy neutrinos. Among them are compact binary coalescences with at least one neutron star, but also core-collapse supernovae or accretion disk instabilities. Two different analyses are presented, combining data from the LIGO and Virgo gravitational-wave detectors with those from the ANTARES and ORCA neutrino telescopes observed during the third observing run of LIGO-Virgo. In the first analysis, selected high-energy neutrino candidates were used as triggers to search for gravitational-wave candidates. In the second analysis, a search was conducted for potential spatial and temporal coincidences between subthreshold high-energy neutrino candidate events and subthreshold gravitational-wave candidates emitted by compact binary coalescence systems. In both searches, no significant coincidences were found. Upper limits on the rate of sources emitting both high-energy neutrinos and gravitational waves are presented. In particular, with the joint search, a joint source rate density upper limit of $8.8\times10^2~\mathrm{ Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ was found for a typical binary neutron star coalescence with a GW emitted energy of $10^{-1}~\rm M_\odot c^2$ and an isotropic energy emitted in neutrinos of $10^{51}~$erg.

papers.title: Data-driven characterisation of variable source light curves with multimodal representation learning
papers.abstract: Surveys such as the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) produce light curves for hundreds of millions of variables. Their characterisation traditionally relies on supervised classifiers with hand-crafted features and curated labels, limiting them to predefined taxonomies and individual surveys. We present a general, survey-agnostic framework that characterises variable sources without labelled training data, producing low-dimensional representations of light curve properties such as amplitude, periodicity, and asymmetry. A multimodal architecture combines two complementary views, a Transformer encoder on raw observations and a convolutional neural network on a generalised Lomb-Scargle periodogram. Each light curve is randomly split into two temporal halves as independent views, and the branches are trained jointly with VICReg to produce embeddings invariant across halves while keeping each dimension informative. We evaluate on 37 006 ZTF sources spanning 14 variable star classes in four broad physical categories. A linear classifier on the frozen 64-dimensional embeddings achieves 77.1% balanced accuracy for classes and 90.5% for broad categories. Combining both branches improves balanced accuracy by up to 14.9 percentage points over the best single modality, confirming their complementarity. Interpretable light curve properties are encoded on distinct dimensions, and within-class analysis reveals physical substructure unresolved by reference labels. Retraining on ZTF g and i bands without modification reproduces the main results, and concatenating multi-band embeddings improves balanced accuracy to 86.1%. The framework needs no labels, phase folding, or survey-specific preprocessing and applies directly to other surveys with different cadences and wavelength coverage.

papers.title: FEAST: Spatially Resolved Star Formation History of the NGC 4485/NGC 4490 System and its Tidal Bridge from JWST/NIRCam Color Magnitude Diagrams
papers.abstract: We present the spatially resolved star formation history (SFH) of the interacting, low-mass, gas-rich galaxy pair NGC 4485/NGC 4490, based on deep JWST/NIRCam imaging obtained as part of the FEAST program. Using resolved stars' near-infrared color-magnitude diagrams (CMDs) and the SFERA 2.0 CMD fitting code, we reconstruct the SFH of the system, including the tidal bridge connecting the two galaxies. We find that recent star formation is widespread across the system, extending beyond the main bodies of the galaxies into the tidal bridge and other off-center areas. In particular, a significant fraction of the recent star formation in NGC 4485 occurs outside its central region. All major regions of the system exhibit two prominent episodes of enhanced star formation, occurring around 0.5-1 Gyr and 10-30 Myr ago, with the tidal bridge showing the largest increase relative to its average star formation rate. These peaks in star formation activity occur a few hundred million years after the epochs of the first and second pericenter passages predicted by independent dynamical models, supporting a scenario in which repeated tidal interactions triggered the observed bursts through gas redistribution and compression. Our results place direct observational constraints on the formation history of NGC 4485/NGC 4490 and provide evidence for the important role of galaxy interactions in driving spatially extended, bursty star formation in low-mass galaxies.

papers.title: Direct Access to Nuclear Photon TMDs with In Situ Probes in Ultraperipheral Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: Resolving local structure in photon distributions is an important goal in probing strong coherent electromagnetic fields. We propose using electron--positron pairs produced in situ in ultraperipheral heavy-ion collisions as dynamical probes to directly extract photon distributions. We define a theoretical reference cross section using the complete tree-level amplitude for two-photon-induced radiative lepton-pair production. When background effects factorize into a scalar Bose-enhancement factor, the ratio of the background-modified to reference differential cross sections, minus unity, yields the photon occupation number at a fixed momentum. Finite bins yield averages weighted by the reference cross section. We specify the conditions under which kinematic selections, acceptance, and radiative corrections preserve this local inversion.

papers.title: Orientation-dependent sensitivity of the all-sky all-frequency gravitational-wave radiometer search to continuous-wave sources
papers.abstract: The all-sky all-frequency (ASAF) gravitational-wave radiometer search cross-correlates the data of two detectors with equal weight on the $+$ and $\times$ tensor polarizations. This is optimal for an unpolarized stochastic background, but not for continuous-wave (CW) sources, whose polarization depends on the inclination angle $\iota$ and the polarization angle $\psi$. Unless the source is seen face-on, the search measures less power than a face-on source with the same intrinsic amplitude, and underestimates its strength. The ratio of the two powers, the projection factor $\mu^2(\iota,\psi)$, is known from earlier radiometer studies. We show how $\mu^2$ enters the ASAF statistic, derive its exact dependence on $\psi$, and prove that its average over orientations is exactly $2/5$, independent of sky position, baseline geometry, noise weighting, and frequency. We apply the formalism to four simulated pulsar signals at four sky positions, with polarization from circular to nearly linear, injected into the LIGO detectors during the second observing run (O2). A nearly edge-on injection is measured with a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $5.20$, below the threshold of $6.19$, while the same signal seen face-on would have an SNR of $31.1 \pm 6.0$. Bayesian upper limits on the strain amplitude $h_0$, marginalized over orientation and calibration uncertainty, are $2.7$ to $2.9$ times the face-on values. For the $505$ sub-threshold candidates of the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run (O4a), the upper limits increase by a factor of $2.5$ to $2.9$, and a source of the same strength would reach threshold only when inclined by less than $34.7^{\circ}$ to $50.3^{\circ}$ from face-on. The measured SNR and the significance of every candidate are unchanged.

papers.title: Surface regolith model of near-Earth asteroid (3200) Phaethon
papers.abstract: The near-Earth asteroid (3200) Phaethon displays activity as it comes close to the Sun and is presumed to be the progenitor of the Geminids meteor shower. Both CM- and CY-meteorites have been suggested as possible meteorite analogues for Phaethon. Previous spectral and polarization measurements of Phaethon indicate possible surface heterogeneity in the regolith properties. By combining mineral components and their size fractions, we present a regolith model for Phaethon that reproduces the spectral, polarization, and geometric albedo measurements presented in various studies, with the aim of quantitatively characterizing the surface material and structure, as well as the regolith heterogeneity. The best fit model able to produce the measurements is constructed from large olivine particles with troilite inclusions and small scale surface roughness, mixed with smaller, porous troilite aggregates comprised of monomers resembling interplanetary dust. Our model suggests that the different spectral and polarization responses of the regolith are caused by changes in the size and amount of the small dark troilite particles. Based on the amount of troilite in the regolith model, we propose that CM-meteorites are the preferable meteorite analogue for Phaethon.

papers.title: Lasting mEMRIs: Signatures of Multiple Black Hole Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals from AGN discs
papers.abstract: Encounters of stellar-mass black holes (sBH) in active galactic nuclei discs naturally form mean-motion resonances of sBH pairs. These mean-motion resonances can be broken close to the central supermassive black hole when gravitational-wave emission dominates over gas torques. We derive a simple condition that depends only on the sBH mass ratio and the resonance index for which a pair of sBH in a mean-motion resonance will remain intact and can be detectable as a multiple Extreme-Mass-Ratio-Inspirals (mEMRIs) in the LISA band. We present for the first time the gravitational-wave strain signatures of a pair of co-migrating sBH in mean-motion resonance, including additional gravitational-wave harmonics associated with orbital conjunctions of the individual EMRIs. The frequency evolution and the associated chirp mass is degenerate with isolated EMRIs of different masses. However, the mEMRI mass ratio is quantised by the resonance order and is larger than the true mass ratio. The degeneracy can be broken if the true sBH mass ratio can be inferred from individual strain amplitudes. We argue that mEMRIs should be common if disc driven EMRIs are to be detected by LISA, with $\sim 10$ mEMRIs per year in the local universe ($z \lesssim 0.2$), highlighting the need to model mEMRI systems in future LISA data analysis.

papers.title: Ballistic mixing: stellar mergers drive internal mixing in extremely massive stars, with implications for proto-globular cluster pollution
papers.abstract: Extremely massive stars, with masses of $10^3$-$10^4$ M$_\odot$, have been proposed as potential sources of the chemical enrichment associated with multiple populations in globular clusters. Early on the main sequence, these stars reach central temperatures of 65 to 75 MK, enabling nucleosynthesis through the CNO, NeNa, and MgAl cycles, producing abundance patterns similar to those observed in the so-called cluster's second population. Stellar mergers are among the leading formation channels for extremely massive stars. In this work, we follow the formation of a $\sim6700$ M$_\odot$ star via 253 stellar mergers, drawn from a direct $N$-body star cluster simulation with properties similar to the densest star clusters observed at redshift $z\sim10$. We evolve each star as a 1D stellar model and construct the merger products from mixing and shock heating prescriptions calibrated to 3D simulations of parabolic collisions. We find that entropy-based mixing efficiently transports nuclear-processed material from the convective core to the envelope, while merger-driven heating promotes chemical homogenization. As a result, the stellar surface becomes enriched with H-burning products, producing abundance patterns consistent with those observed in globular cluster multiple populations and supporting the role of merger-formed extremely massive stars as potential sources of early chemical enrichment in proto-globular cluster-like conditions.

papers.title: Magnetic monopoles produced by first-order phase transition
papers.abstract: We present the first 3D lattice simulations of magnetic monopole production from a first-order phase transition, using the Press-Ryden-Spergel method, capturing the subsequent annihilation stage and the entry into the scaling regime in an expanding universe. We establish the quantitative relationship between the initial bubble number and the residual monopole abundance, and calculate the magnetic field and gravitational wave power spectra sourced by monopole dynamics. Crucially, we find that the magnetic field spectrum displays a steep $k^{-5}$ decline beyond the monopole size $w_M$, whereas the peak of the gravitational wave spectrum aligns with the scale of the mean monopole separation $d_M$, governed by $k^3$ and $k^{-3}$ scalings on the low- and high-wavenumber sides of the peak, respectively. However, since the resulting magnetic field strength is excluded by blazar observations, magnetic monopoles cannot be the origin of primordial cosmic magnetic fields. Finally, we determine the allowed monopole mass under the constraints of the Parker bound ($m_M\lesssim2.18\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{GeV}$) and dark matter abundance ($m_M\lesssim1.58\times10^{12}\,\mathrm{GeV}$).

papers.title: Heavy Pseudo-Dirac Doublet Dark Matter and Non-Thermal Leptogenesis in Light of the LZ Event
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent LZ candidate nuclear-recoil event, we study pseudo-Dirac electroweak doublet dark matter in the mass range $10^2$--$10^4\,\mathrm{TeV}$, where bounds from searches for neutrinos produced by dark matter annihilation in the Sun can be evaded. To suppress the excessive thermal relic abundance, we consider freeze-out during inflaton domination followed by entropy production during reheating. We examine whether this cosmological history can also accommodate non-thermal leptogenesis. Our analysis includes dark matter production through the emission of virtual electroweak gauge bosons in right-handed-neutrino decays and through thermalization cascades. Our estimates suggest that the two scenarios can be reconciled if dark matter pair emission in right-handed-neutrino decays is kinematically forbidden and cascade production is sufficiently suppressed. Such a realization, however, requires enhanced CP violation, typically involving fine-tuning in the seesaw mechanism or the right-handed-neutrino mass spectrum.

papers.title: Spin - resolved momentum distributions and vortex evolution in multiphoton pair production within a modified two-level model
papers.abstract: We investigate spin-resolved momentum distributions and phase vortices in multiphoton electron-positron pair production within a modified two-level model. This model retains the diagonal spinor inner-product terms neglected in the adiabatic approximation, thereby inducing spin-resolved transverse asymmetries in the momentum distribution. For a circularly polarized pulse, the handedness determines the winding direction of the quantized vortices, whereas for a linearly polarized pulse, the phase distribution exhibits nodal lines rather than quantized vortices. For two time-delayed circularly polarized pulses, the time delay introduces a relative phase that governs the multiphoton interference, which in turn drives the vortex evolution in each spin configuration. These results demonstrate that pulse polarization and time delay enable coherent control over vortex topology in pair production.

papers.title: simesh: A Python Framework for Quantitative Analysis of Native AMR Data from MPI-AMRVAC
papers.abstract: Adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) is widely used in large-scale astrophysical simulations, but the resulting multilevel data are challenging to analyze quantitatively. We present simesh, an independent Python framework for quantitative analysis of cell-centered fields on block-structured AMR meshes. The current implementation targets three-dimensional Cartesian datasets from MPI-AMRVAC and compatible AGILE snapshots, preserving the native AMR hierarchy and connecting complementary scientific diagnostics within a common numerical representation. The framework combines Python workflow interfaces with compiled Cython kernels, supporting efficient analysis on AMR meshes. We compare native AMR analysis with a VTK point-data conversion and uniform-grid resampling, which shows that changes in data association, interpolation support, and differentiation scale affect both sampled magnetic fields and derived current densities. Small differences in the sampled primary field can become more pronounced in derivative-based quantities, particularly near coarse-fine interfaces. The applications combine field diagnostics, tracing, regional statistics, and line-of-sight integration on the same native AMR representation. simesh makes these operations available through reusable Python interfaces for reproducible analysis of multiscale simulation data.

papers.title: Enhanced Mass Transfer from Extended Shock-Supported Stellar Chromospheres
papers.abstract: Mass transfer (MT) in binary systems is a crucial and complex process. Even before the donor's photosphere fills its Roche lobe, matter from its outer atmosphere can reach the inner Lagrange point, thus initiating interaction in the so-called optically thin phase. Most existing models account for a very tenuous atmosphere supported by thermal gas pressure, thus predicting very little MT until the donor fills its Roche lobe. However, recent hydrodynamic simulations of giant stars suggest that shock-driven outflows can create substantially thicker "chromospheres'' extending to a few stellar radii. In this work, we derive a simple analytic model for a shock-supported chromosphere in a binary potential and calculate the corresponding MT rate. We also implement our prescription in the stellar evolution code MESA. We show that chromospheric MT rates can be orders of magnitude higher than prior estimates for optically thin MT, especially for stars high on the red giant or asymptotic giant branch. This allows for substantial accretion before Roche lobe overflow, both for systems that undergo stable mass transfer and for systems that go through common envelope evolution. Thus, for a given initial binary configuration, this may alter the final period and component masses compared to those predicted classically. Our model is similar to Wind Roche-lobe Overflow, but it is physically rather than empirically motivated. We discuss implications for various post-interaction binaries that can be tested with population synthesis studies and observed binary populations. Additionally, we have identified an inaccuracy in the current implementation of the optically-thin Ritter 1988 prescription in MESA, which we correct.

papers.title: B-fields In STar-forming Region Observations (BISTRO): Dual-Wavelength Constraints on Size-Dependent Grain Alignment in Star-Forming Regions
papers.abstract: We compared 450 and 850 $\mu$m POL-2 observations from the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope at $12.6''$ resolution. The median absolute difference in polarization angle between bands is $6.7^\circ$ across 21 regions. For total intensity $I\propto\nu^\alpha$ and polarized intensity $PI\propto\nu^\gamma$, 24-27 of 35 regions have $\gamma<\alpha$, allowing for $3\sigma$ limits on weak polarized intensities. The median $\gamma-\alpha$ is $-0.51$, ranging from $-0.57$ to $-0.45$ under these limits. The ratio of polarization fractions is $P_{450}/P_{850}=0.69\pm0.02_{\rm sys}\pm0.03_{\rm stat}$, with no detected dependence on the angle difference. We suggest that the dependence of alignment on grain size offers the simplest explanation of these findings. For optically thin components sharing a polarization angle and opacity law, temperature mixing reproduces the median $-0.51$ only if the warm dust is polarized less efficiently than the cold dust. If the cold dust is at 10 K or warmer and the warm dust at 40 K or cooler, the median requires a ratio of warm to cold effective polarization efficiencies $r\lesssim0.18$. We tested mixtures with opacity index $\beta=2$ in four fields against Herschel dust temperatures and Green Bank Ammonia Survey kinetic temperatures. We assumed equal gas and dust temperatures, ammonia tracing cold gas, and model ranges of 3-20 K for cold dust and 25-40 K for warm dust carrying at most half the mass. Mixtures matching both temperatures cannot reproduce $\gamma-\alpha$ within $1\sigma$ in three fields, including OMC 2 tentatively, even for $r=0$. Allowing warm dust at 10-100 K and up to 95% of the mass permits solutions only for $r\leq0.041$. To explain these three fields by temperature mixing, we need wider model ranges and a very strong contrast in polarization efficiency. The origin of this contrast remains undetermined.

papers.title: Tomimatsu--Sato $=2$ Solution in Kaluza--Klein Theory
papers.abstract: We construct the Kaluza-Klein electric dressing of the Tomimatsu-Sato $\delta=2$ vacuum spacetime by uplifting to five dimensions, boosting along the compact direction and reducing to Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton theory with coupling $a=\sqrt3$. It carries a nontrivial dilaton, unlike the known Einstein-Maxwell charged and magnetized Tomimatsu-Sato solutions. At leading order it shares the mass-charge-dilaton relations and gyromagnetic ratio $g=2-\tanh^2\alpha$ of the boosted Kerr black hole; the seed first shows up in the quadrupole. Using Mayerson's non-vacuum Geroch-Hansen multipoles, we derive the exact law $M_2(\alpha)=\frac12(1+\cosh^2\alpha)M_2^{(0)}$, so the $\delta=2$ quadrupole excess $\Delta M_2=-\frac14p^2m^2M$ survives every boost. In the Kodama-Hikida picture the Weyl segment $\rho=0$, $|z|<\kappa$ is a singular rod with degenerate Killing horizons at its endpoints. There the boost function equals $\cosh\alpha$, so the near-horizon geometry is a constant rescaling of the seed's: the horizons stay degenerate and non-rotating, their areas and Komar angular momenta scale by $\cosh\alpha$, and the electric potential is $\frac12\tanh\alpha$. The electric flux through any closed surface is $\sinh\alpha\cosh\alpha$ times the enclosed seed Komar mass, so the horizons and the ring singularity are uncharged and the rod carries all the charge; the boost-invariant identity $M-\Phi_eQ=m$ follows. The ergosurface stays at $f=0$; a new curvature-singular boundary appears at $f=\coth^2\alpha$, where the Kaluza-Klein circle becomes null. As the seed potential $f$ is unbounded above near the ring, it exists for every nonzero boost: unlike for Kerr, no Kaluza-Klein boost of TS$_2$ is a spacelike reduction everywhere. The excised region is compact, has the ring on its boundary and never reaches the horizons. Charging pointwise strengthens the causality violation near the rod.

papers.title: B-fields In STar-forming Region Observations (BISTRO): Technical Foundations for Quantitative 450/850 $$m JCMT SCUBA-2/POL-2 Polarimetry
papers.abstract: We present five technical validations of SCUBA-2/POL-2 polarimetry on the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope at 450 and 850 $\mu$m, using 174 archival fields in 69 molecular cloud regions and subsets appropriate to each test. Extended-source calibration avoids a deterministic shift of $\Delta\beta=-1.05$ in the dust emissivity index $\beta$ that would result from calibrating extended emission using peak brightness. We modeled Stokes $I$ noise with additive and signal-dependent components. The measured median ratio of surface-brightness noise at 450/850 $\mu$m is 25. Independent tests of Stokes $Q,U$ noise support approximately equal additive variances and weak error correlations, providing a basis for propagating polarization uncertainties. Corrections determined for individual fields reduce additive zero-level offsets of order $1$ mJy arcsec$^{-2}$ in the 450 $\mu$m Stokes $Q$ and $U$ intensities. The three-step regression leaves a median combined residual amplitude of $0.07$ mJy arcsec$^{-2}$. Independent comparisons with SOFIA/HAWC+ at 154 and 214 $\mu$m support the correction in strongly affected fields. We matched the 450 $\mu$m maps to the modeled 850 $\mu$m beam and the common $12.6''$-$300''$ range of angular scales. We compared three reductions of the same 450 $\mu$m observations across 30 sources. Taking the median angular residual relative to the final product for each source, we find that beam matching reduces the median over sources from $6.3^\circ$ to $4.7^\circ$. After matching, 29 of the 30 sources have median residuals below $10^\circ$. We also quantified how residual $Q/U$ offsets propagate in ratios of polarization fractions, differences in spectral indices, and polarization angles. These validations provide procedures and quantitative references for interpreting POL-2 measurements and combining them with polarimetry at other wavelengths.

papers.title: General Relativistic Simulations of the Nonlinear Evolution of r-modes in Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: The r-modes in rotating neutron stars are a promising source of continuous gravitational waves, and may grow or be excited to amplitudes $\alpha\lesssim1$. We perform general relativistic simulations of nonlinear $l=|m|=2$ r-modes in a rapidly rotating neutron star with spin frequency $f_{spin}\approx792$ Hz, relaxing the Cowling and small-$\alpha$ approximations. The star is idealised as an unmagnetised, one-component, perfect fluid with a polytropic equation of state. The r-mode frequency is measured to be $f_{r-mode}=1014$ Hz for initial amplitude $\alpha_0=0.2$. The dimensionless frequency $\kappa\approx0.7197$ agrees with an estimate from linear perturbation theory to within 1.7%. $f_{r-mode}$ increases quadratically with amplitude, and $\kappa$ decreases by 3.4% across simulations where $\alpha_0$ is varied through the range $0.2\leq\alpha_0\leq1.2$. The gravitational wave strain calculated from the Newman-Penrose scalar implies $h_{r-mode}\approx9.7\times10^{-22}$ at $10$ kpc for $\alpha_0=0.2$, which agrees with Einstein's quadrupole formula to within 35%. We also report on nonlinear phenomena observed in our simulations, e.g. differential rotation, amplitude decay, and signatures of nonlinear mode coupling in the spacetime oscillations.

papers.title: How general relativity stacks up: Testing gravity by coherently combining gravitational-wave observations
papers.abstract: A core mission of gravitational-wave astronomy is to test general relativity (GR) in the high-curvature, high-velocity regime. The field has already seen significant progress in this space, though a remaining challenge is how to combine data from a population of binary mergers. This can both boost the significance of potential GR violations, and develop a phenomenological picture of how deviations manifest in different mergers. We propose a framework to coherently combine gravitational-wave measurements to build a population-level test of physics beyond GR. We assume that deviations from GR are (i) strongest near the merger, (ii) vary smoothly with the total mass of the binary, and (iii) are most prominent in the $\ell=|m|=2$ mode. While these assumptions do not describe every possible deviation of GR, they provide us with a plausible starting point upon which a more general framework can be built. We apply our framework to 28 high signal-to-noise ratio binary black hole mergers from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's Fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, finding no evidence for deviations from GR. Our framework allows one to show how deviations could vary as a function of total mass of the system. We argue that such a reconstruction can be used to convincingly distinguish between systematic waveform errors and genuine GR violations.

papers.title: Parity-odd CMB Correlations induced by a Chiral Gravitational Wave Background
papers.abstract: We investigate weak lensing effects of a chiral gravitational wave background (GWB) as a new mechanism for generating parity-odd correlations in the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Accounting for both photon deflection and polarization rotation, we derive the resulting parity-odd EB and TB angular power spectra. For representative GWB energy density spectra, we find parameter choices that provide good fits to existing measurements. This mechanism provides a potential observational probe of chiral GWB, which can arise in a wide range of theoretical scenarios.

papers.title: $$Gundam: a unified framework for point-redshift and PDF-aware spatial correlation functions
papers.abstract: Context. Photometric-redshift uncertainties redistribute galaxy pairs along the line of sight (LOS), diluting spatial clustering measurements. Propagating full redshift probability density functions (PDFs) through standard pair-count estimators remains computationally demanding. Aims. We present $\nu$Gundam, a unified framework to propagate radial PDFs at the pair-count level while retaining a common interface for exact, compressed, and stochastic projected-clustering calculations. Methods. The code implements four modes: exact empirical-PDF integration, Gaussian-mixture compression, Monte Carlo (MC) sampling, and a quantile-compression method. All modes accumulate pair counts on a resolved ($r_\mathrm{p},\pi$) grid, from which $\xi(r_\mathrm{p},\pi)$ and $w_\mathrm{p}(r_\mathrm{p};\Pi)$ are reconstructed. We validate these with DESI galaxies and CosmoDC2 mocks. Results. The PDF-aware modes produce nearly indistinguishable LOS redistribution kernels, while point-photo-$z$ estimates discard probabilistic pair information. Radial uncertainty mainly redistributes the clustering signal to larger $\pi$; the depth required to recover the truth projection scales with the pairwise radial dispersion. For practical settings, MC, quantile, and Gaussian-mixture compression reproduce the exact result with fractional RMS residuals below 5%. Applied to DESI Bright Galaxy Survey samples, MC sampling recovers spectroscopic clustering shapes and relative amplitudes for $r_\mathrm{p}\gtrsim0.8\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ using sample-dependent recovery depths of ~400 and ~$180\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ for red and blue galaxies. Conclusions. Projected clustering with redshift PDFs is a pair-redistribution problem. When propagated consistently, the signal is recovered accurately and efficiently. The integration depth is sample dependent and should be part of the measurement definition rather than a fixed choice.

papers.title: The MAGE Project: Size Evolution and Disk Formation in Massive Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn
papers.abstract: We investigate size evolution and disk formation with a new suite of eleven cosmological zoom-in simulations, Massive Assembly of Galaxies in the Early universe (MAGE), run with RAMSES at $\sim10\,\mathrm{pc}$ resolution until $z\simeq9$. The target galaxies span stellar masses of $M_\star\simeq2\times10^8$-$3\times10^{10}\,M_\odot$ at $z=9$. The stellar half-mass radius grows steeply with stellar mass at low masses, turns over near $M_\star\simeq5\times10^9\,M_\odot$, and evolves weakly with redshift. The intrinsic UV sizes in MAGE overlap the compact end of observed distributions, including the compact strong-line systems, but not the more extended population at $z>9$. Dust, PSF-limited size measurements, and our overdense environments may contribute to this offset. In the simulations, stars dominate the mass within the half-mass radius above $M_\star\simeq5\times10^8\,M_\odot$, where the central circular speed exceeds a characteristic stellar-feedback scale. Outflows are then increasingly retained within the galaxy, consistent with gas recycling on galactic rather than halo scales, which sustains central gas supply and drives a compaction-like central buildup. The turnover in size at $M_\star\simeq5\times10^9\,M_\odot$ coincides with rapid growth of rotational support to $v/\sigma\simeq1.5$-$3$ in star-forming gas and stars younger than 10Myr, as the central circular speed exceeds the halo virial speed, which the star-forming gas velocity dispersion tracks. The subsequent low central gas fraction, declining central star formation, and younger outskirts suggest the onset of inside-out quenching.

papers.title: Dual-Phase Flow Matching for Probabilistic Source Detection and Measurement in Astronomical Images
papers.abstract: Using the largest digital camera ever built, the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory's 10-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will image over half the night sky. Most astronomical analyses of LSST data operate not on images but on catalogs derived from them: tables of light sources detailing their positions, fluxes (colors and brightnesses), and types (e.g., star, galaxy). At LSST's imaging depths, light sources often overlap visually, so the configuration of sources in each image is itself uncertain. Nevertheless, LSST's cataloging pipeline commits to a single source configuration, which can bias downstream analyses. Here, we instead approximate a posterior distribution over source configurations. Our posterior approximation is a continuous-time Markov process (CTMP) fitted by generator matching, an extension of flow matching to non-Euclidean state spaces. This CTMP generates a source configuration in two phases: it detects light sources in the first and measures them in the second. On simulated LSST-like data, the proposed method produces better posterior approximations than five comparison methods: two Markov chain Monte Carlo methods that run thousands of times more slowly at survey scales; two neural posterior estimation methods; and one ablation of the proposed method that lacks the dual-phase structure. Applied to LSST Data Preview 1 (DP1), the first public release of Rubin imaging, the proposed method alone recovers small-scale galaxy clustering in agreement with higher-resolution Hubble imaging and reports uncertainty that remains calibrated against that reference as blending increases. We deliver a probabilistic catalog of the Extended Chandra Deep Field South region, one of the most extensively studied extragalactic fields, and use it to characterize the galaxy color-magnitude distribution.

papers.title: Not so Fast: Revised Calibration of SIDM Core Collapse
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) haloes undergo gravothermal evolution whose late-time behaviour is central to predictions for dense substructure and black-hole seed formation. We revisit the calibration of this evolution using a new spherical Direct Simulation Monte Carlo code, SphDSMC, which follows spherically symmetric SIDM systems without force softening and to substantially higher central densities than standard N-body simulations. We compare SphDSMC calculations with conventional N-body simulations and with one-dimensional gravothermal fluid models. We show that N-body results converge to SphDSMC only for softening lengths significantly smaller than those normally adopted for collisionless simulations, and that allowing multiple scatterings per particle per time step does not introduce significant errors when implemented appropriately. Calibrating the gravothermal fluid equations against SphDSMC, we find that the commonly used harmonic interpolation between the long- and short-mean-free-path conductivities is inaccurate. A gentler transition, however, yields excellent agreement for NFW haloes over a range of concentrations and truncation radii, with a single long-mean-free-path conductivity parameter. The revised calibration gives a long-mean-free-path collapse time that is somewhat shorter than previous estimates, but we show that collapse slows dramatically once the core becomes optically thick. We provide fitting functions for the late-time evolution and argue that black-hole seed formation by SIDM gravothermal collapse has generally been underestimated in duration, making it unlikely to explain the massive high-redshift black holes inferred from JWST observations without additional physics.

papers.title: Can we constrain the binary neutron star merger time from kilonova light curves?
papers.abstract: The joint observation of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary neutron star (BNS) merger (GW170817), together with a short Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB 170817A) and a kilonova (KN, AT2017gfo), marked the birth of multimessenger astronomy with GWs, and demonstrated the informative power of multimessenger observations. More BNS merger and KN detections are expected , thanks to the increasing sensitivity of GW detectors and the advent of new electromagnetic facilities such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. However, the association between a BNS merger and a KN might not be trivial: the detection of a KN might not coincide with the onset of the EM emission, making it difficult to define a temporal window to assess the coincidence with a GW event. In this work we investigate the possibility to constrain the BNS merger time from KN light curves, exploring different observing conditions and with focus on the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. We used different KN models and different inference frameworks to simulate and fit KN light curves. We explored different cadences and wavelength coverages for observations, to investigate how the different observing conditions can affect the capability to recover the BNS merger time. The tests performed also include real data related to AT2017gfo, plus a few GRBs that have been associated to possible KN candidates. We find that, under realistic observing conditions with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, the BNS merger time can be recovered with a precision of 5.5 days (90\% CI) with a best-case scenario with an accuracy of 0.18 day and a precision of 0.74 day (90 \% CI). Results can slightly improve (by $\sim$ 5 \%) if the source redshift is available. Upper limits near the merger time can also improve the results, reducing the width of the posterior by $\sim60$ \%. The BNS merger time estimate could also benefit from EM follow-up observations with other telescopes.

papers.title: Constraints on Reionization from Planck Low-$$ EE Polarization and the Lyman-Series Forests
papers.abstract: CMB measurements tightly constrain the Thomson scattering optical depth ($\tau_{\rm es}$), but they still permit a broad range of degenerate reionization histories. Incorporating Lyman-series forest constraints on the end of reionization can alleviate the degeneracy and narrow the range of allowed histories. We explore this effect using forest measurements combined with full Planck likelihoods. We apply upper limits on the neutral fraction at $4.9\lesssim z\lesssim6.9$ derived from the dark pixel fraction, as well as a lower limit at $z=5.8$ from damping-wing-like features on the edges of long dark gaps in stacked forest spectra. We find that neither the choice of parametric vs. non-parametric reionization model, nor the choice among different forest data combinations, produces a significant shift in $\tau_{\rm es}$ or the other cosmological parameters. Instead, forest constraints primarily redistribute $\tau_{\rm es}$ in redshift. Combining dark pixel, damping-wing-like, and CMB measurements, we find $z_{50}=7.7^{+0.7}_{-0.8}$ and a 95\% upper limit of $\Delta z_{90}<11.4$ for the midpoint and duration of reionization, respectively. The asymmetry of the reionization history ($A_z$) is not well constrained by these data. Stronger constraints can be obtained using Ly$\alpha$ forest measurements of the mean IGM photoionization rate, at the cost of requiring more detailed modeling. Using a new semi-analytic reionization model, we obtain (model-dependent) constraints of $z_{50} = 7.4^{+0.2}_{-0.3}$, $\Delta z_{90}=6.0^{+0.8}_{-1.0}$, and $A_z = 2.4^{+0.3}_{-0.7}$. We also find evidence that the ionizing emissivity of reionization sources declines after $z=7-8$, perhaps signaling a decline in the escape fraction and/or the onset of a feedback process. Our results motivate the development of forest likelihood products and fast forward models for its transmission statistics.

papers.title: PIANISTpy: A JAX-based Python package for velocity-anisotropic astrophysical equilibrium models
papers.abstract: The hierarchical assembly of dark matter haloes and galaxies via mergers and anisotropic mass accretion naturally imprints non-trivial velocity anisotropy onto haloes and galaxies, an empirical fact emerging from cosmological simulations. However, dynamical studies based on idealised numerical simulations typically assume isotropic velocity distributions for the systems studied. This is mainly because no tools exist to construct anisotropic initial conditions with fully self-consistent (i.e., physical and instability-free) truncation boundary conditions for finite spatial extents. Here we present the first such analytical framework that performs truncation in phase space, with two distinct approaches to guarantee either the monotonicity of output distribution functions or identical truncated density profiles. We additionally present the open-source JAX-based GPU-accelerated Python package PIANISTpy (Particle Initial conditions with ANISoTropy) for constructing spherical, non-rotating initial conditions, supporting arbitrary double-power-law analytical radial density profiles and a library of analytical anisotropy profiles. This framework further permits the construction of systems with non-analytical anisotropy profiles via an arbitrary linear superposition of all implemented analytical anisotropy models as basis functions. PIANISTpy also outputs 3D velocity profiles and line-of-sight-integrated observables with end-to-end differentiability for rapid gradient-based Monte Carlo inference, and self-consistent local dark matter velocity distributions of anisotropic haloes beyond the unphysical Maxwell-Boltzmann simplification adopted in terrestrial detection experiments. We discuss use cases and demonstrate PIANISTpy's orders-of-magnitude higher numerical solver accuracy and superior dynamical stability of particle initial conditions relative to existing tools, including galpy and AGAMA.

papers.title: Gravothermal Evolution of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Halos across Knudsen Numbers
papers.abstract: If the dark matter self-interacts elastically via a light mediator, then at relative velocities above a scale $w$ dictated by particle physics parameters, the cross section scales as $\sigma \propto v^{-4}$. Depending on the value of $w$, the self-interaction cross section in low-mass halos could be (much) larger than has been previously studied extensively. We perform kinetic simulations of isolated self-interacting dark matter halos using the code KiSS-SIDM for a wide range of halo masses, concentrations, and cross sections from $50 \,\mathrm{cm}^2 \, \mathrm{g}^{-1}$ to $250{,}000 \, \mathrm{cm}^2 \, \mathrm{g}^{-1}$, including several velocity-dependent and fully differential (anisotropic) cross sections. We demonstrate that for idealized NFW halos the collapse time can be predicted from the Knudsen number at the scale radius of the halo. We perform similar calculations for halos extracted from cosmological simulations using either $N$-body (collisionless) or SPH (strongly collisional) dynamics, and then evolve cutouts with KiSS-SIDM. For these halos, the collapse times differ from the idealized NFW simulations by up to a factor of a few. Further, we calibrate a hydrostatic fluid model to these results, which solves the structure equations as a boundary value problem via two-point shooting. The fluid calculation predicts that for velocity-independent cross sections, a convective region of the halo develops late in the collapse. The collapse times agree well between the kinetic simulations and the fluid code, especially in the velocity-independent case. The density profiles agree well in some cases, which include all of the velocity-dependent cross section runs.

papers.title: Unveiling the correlation between the UV 2175 A dust attenuation bump, PAH emission, and gas-phase metallicity at cosmic noon
papers.abstract: The UV 2175 \r{A} attenuation bump is one of the most prominent yet poorly understood features of galaxy attenuation curves. Its main candidate carrier is polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) molecules, which are more prevalent in high-metallicity environments. We present the first systematic study of the relationship between PAH abundance and the UV bump in 49 galaxies at cosmic noon (1.5 < z < 2.7), examining its dependence on stellar mass, star formation rate (SFR), and V-band optical depth. For 19 galaxies, we also investigate gas-phase metallicity using oxygen abundances. We measure the bump amplitude from VLT/MUSE spectroscopy and derive galaxy properties, including the PAH-to-dust mass fraction $q_{\rm PAH}$, through spectral energy distribution fitting with Prospector, combining JWST/NIRCam and JWST/MIRI photometry. Oxygen abundances are derived from strong-line diagnostics using Keck/MOSFIRE and JWST/NIRSpec data. We find a positive correlation between bump amplitude $E_{\rm bump}$ and $q_{\rm PAH}$ (Spearman $\rho = 0.60$). UV bumps are rarely detected at low $q_{\rm PAH}$, supporting PAHs as their primary carriers. Both $E_{\rm bump}$ and $q_{\rm PAH}$ correlate with stellar mass, oxygen abundance, and optical depth, and anticorrelate with specific SFR, suggesting that PAHs and the UV bump are suppressed in low-metallicity, dust-poor, and/or intensely star-forming environments. This is consistent with PAH destruction in environments with limited dust shielding and/or strong radiation fields. A principal component analysis of $E_{\rm bump}$, $q_{\rm PAH}$, optical depth, specific SFR, and oxygen abundance explains 97% of the variance, suggesting that previously reported correlations with stellar mass reflect an underlying dependence on metallicity. Finally, variations in dust geometry may explain the wide range of bump amplitudes (0-0.5 mag) at high $q_{\rm PAH}$.

papers.title: A Hybrid Neural Network Emulator for M1 Neutrino Reaction Rates in Binary Neutron Star Merger Simulations
papers.abstract: We present a neural network emulator for the bns_nurates library, which computes neutrino reaction rates used in binary neutron star merger simulations. Following a hybrid strategy, we emulate only the computationally dominant two-dimensional reactions---pair processes, bremsstrahlung, and inelastic neutrino-electron scattering---while evaluating the inexpensive one-dimensional processes still with bns_nurates. We find that the emulator reproduces the opacities to within a few percent across the relevant thermodynamic conditions and accelerates their evaluation by roughly an order of magnitude. When deployed in a global Athenak binary neutron star merger simulation, it recovers the remnant structure, neutrino luminosities, and ejecta composition of a reference run using the full bns_nurates library, at approximately half the overall cost

papers.title: A combined HST and JWST analysis of the stellar population in Draco II
papers.abstract: Draco II (Dra II) is one of the faintest and most metal-poor Milky Way satellites known, yet its nature as either an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy or an extended globular cluster remains debated. We perform a photometric analysis of the stellar population of Dra II reducing deep multi-band observations from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). We select Dra II member stars based on their proper motions and photometric quality criteria. For the first time, optical and infrared photometry are combined to produce a stellar catalogue reaching 50 percent completeness at $F814W = 26.5$ mag (corresponding to the absolute magnitude $M_{F814W} = 10.1$ mag). The colour-magnitude diagram confirms that Dra II hosts an old stellar population with an age of $13.5_{-1.5}^{+1.7}$ Gyr at a distance of $19.2\pm0.9$ kpc. We measure an $\alpha$-enhanced stellar population with a low mean metallicity of $[\rm Fe/H]_{CaHK} = -2.38 \pm 0.17$ dex and confirm the presence of an intrinsic metallicity spread of $\sigma_{[\rm Fe/H]} = 0.85 \pm 0.13$ dex. We identify 10 unresolved main-sequence binary stars in the HST catalogue with mass ratios $q > 0.5$ in the mass range $0.43<0.71$, corresponding to a binary fraction of $f_{bin}^{q>0.5} = 0.21 \pm 0.07$. This value is higher than those typically observed in globular clusters and lies near the upper range measured in open clusters. The stellar mass function is best modelled by a single power law with a slope of $1.53\pm0.26$ over the mass range $0.13$--$0.77\ M_\odot$. We find no evidence of mass segregation. Consistent results are obtained independently from the JWST catalogue. Combining these findings strongly suggests that Draco II is best classified as an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy rather than a globular cluster.

papers.title: Discovery of a Broad-Line Active Galactic Nucleus at $z = 9.98$
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has uncovered a previously unexplored population of faint active galactic nuclei (AGNs) in the early Universe. We present MoM-BL-z10 at $z=9.9837\pm0.0009$, identified through a systematic search for broad-line AGNs at $z\geq6$ using public JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra from the DAWN JWST Archive. The PRISM spectrum exhibits a broad component in H$\beta$ at 5.35 microns. A narrow+broad Gaussian fit yields a broad H$\beta$ detection at S/N = 3.87, with FWHM = $3480^{+2040}_{-950}$ km s$^{-1}$ and $L_{{\rm H}\beta,{\rm broad}}=1.25^{+0.33}_{-0.31}\times10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$. The detection of [Ne III] $\lambda3870$ and the high [Ne III]/[O II] and [O III]/H$\beta$ ratios further support the AGN interpretation. Its rest-frame UV and optical continuum slopes, compact NIRCam morphology, and a tentative MIRI F770W detection suggest similarities to Little Red Dots (LRDs). The broad H$\beta$ detection enables the first virial SMBH mass estimate at $z\sim10$. We derive $M_{\rm BH}=3.6^{+5.8}_{-1.7}\times10^7 M_\odot$ and $\lambda_{\rm Edd}=0.11^{+0.10}_{-0.07}$ using the standard single-epoch virial calibration and quasar bolometric correction. We also consider an alternative scenario adopting the LRD-specific bolometric correction and assuming $\lambda_{\rm Edd}=1$, which yields $M_{\rm BH}=2.1^{+0.6}_{-0.5}\times10^6 M_\odot$. Under either scenario, the inferred SMBH mass at a cosmic age of only 470 Myr highlights the challenge of rapid BH growth in the early Universe, suggesting super-Eddington accretion from a stellar-mass seed or a more massive seed. As the highest-redshift broad-line AGN identified to date, MoM-BL-z10 provides a new observational benchmark for understanding the early growth of supermassive black holes.

papers.title: Simulation-Informed High-Velocity Dark Matter in the Effective Theory of Direct Detection
papers.abstract: The interpretation and reach of direct detection (DD) experiments depend sensitively on the local dark matter (DM) velocity distribution, particularly its high-velocity tail. This tail is crucial for elastic scattering at low DM masses or large momentum transfers, and for inelastic upscattering, where additional kinetic energy is needed to overcome the mass splitting. In practice, however, phenomenological studies typically rely either on the Standard Halo Model (SHM) or, when an enhanced high-velocity tail contributes to the scattering rate, on the single simulation that includes a large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) analogue, Au-25, whose debris reaches ~ 950\kms. In this work, we instead build on a previously presented empirically-motivated reconstruction method, to construct the local DM velocity distribution, using stellar kinematics from the Gaia space telescope. We combine this reconstructed Milky Way component with the best LMC analog in the FIRE-2 simulations, and find no local DM faster than ~ 900\kms. We compare the resulting distribution with the two commonly used benchmarks, the SHM and Au-25. We then study how these different velocity distributions affect the interpretation of DD searches across all operators of the non-relativistic effective field theory of DM--nucleon interactions, for both elastic and inelastic DM. As an illustrative application, we consider the high-energy event observed in the LUX-ZEPLIN extended search. Requiring the event to remain compatible with the absence of signal in the surrounding energy sidebands, we observe the inferred inelastic DM mass splitting can be shifted by up to $\sim 130$~keV depending on the assumed high-velocity tail. Higher-resolution simulations of the high-velocity DM population reaching the detector will therefore be crucial for interpreting a future signal and setting robust limits on DM interactions.

papers.title: Poisson Clustering and Seed Effect of PBHs: Implications for Microlensing, Gravitational Waves, Little Red Dots and Ultra-Faint Dwarf Galaxies
papers.abstract: The existence of primordial black holes (PBHs) could have significant effects on the formation of cosmic structures through both the seed effect and the Poisson effect. For an extended PBH mass function, this should lead to dark virialised bound clusters of black holes with modest mass, together with central black holes of larger mass. We consider the combination of three effects: the inevitable gravitational binding of small-scale inhomogeneities due to Poisson and seed fluctuations; the dilution through dynamical heating of all clusters smaller than around $10^{6}\,M_{\odot}$; the survival of clusters in the outer Galactic halo (i.e. towards the Magellanic Clouds) but their destruction in the central halo region through tidal disruption and collisions. We examine the implications of this for the constraints on the fraction of dark matter in PBHs from microlensing surveys and gravitational-wave events. Although the clustering of PBHs with the expected mass and radius is unlikely to relax the microlensing limits, the decline of the Galactic rotation curve might do so, allowing much of the dark matter to be in solar-mass PBHs formed at the quantum chromodynamics transition. We also emphasise that binary merger rates must be revised: binaries formed in PBH clusters can dominate the merger rate, which may be compatible with the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA gravitational-wave limits if PBHs provide the dark matter. More positively, Ultra-Faint Dwarf Galaxies and Little Red Dots might arise through a combination of the seed and Poisson effects. Our conclusions could be modified for PBHs produced from primordial fluctuations with exponential non-Gaussian tails, since the clustering would then exceed the Poissonian prediction, opening up new possibilities to explain dark matter with solar-mass PBHs.

papers.title: The Balmer Absorber Strength Problem of Little Red Dots
papers.abstract: Little Red Dots (LRDs) commonly show Balmer absorption features. Some observed LRD spectra have weaker absorption in H$\alpha$ than in H$\beta$, in apparent contradiction to atomic physics according to standard attenuation models. This tension is naturally resolved when one considers emission from the absorbing medium itself, which is ignored in the standard model: when the Balmer absorption is optically thick, a non-negligible source function could fill in the H$\alpha$ absorption trough and reduce its observed absorption equivalent width (EW). With proof-of-concept photoionization models we show that the source function of H$\alpha$ could be systematically stronger than that of H$\beta$. This is due to radiative trapping preferentially populating the $n=3$ level of neutral hydrogen, which operates efficiently when the medium is optically thick to H$\alpha$ but not very optically thick to Paschen-$\alpha$. Such line-dependent source functions could lead to significant corrections to the expected EW and selectively weaken H$\alpha$ absorption, consistent with observations. Quantitatively, this depends on the distance of the absorbing medium and its internal structure, providing a new diagnostic of the environment around LRDs. Future modeling of the absorbers may also potentially open a new avenue for estimating the mass of the central engine.

papers.title: Chemical abundance patterns at z=1-7: Carbon, Nitrogen, Neon, Sulphur, and Argon abundances from JWST spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The relative abundances of chemical elements in the interstellar medium (ISM) trace the history of star formation and chemical enrichment in galaxies. We investigate the abundance patterns of carbon (C), nitrogen (N), neon (Ne), sulfur (S), and argon (Ar) in star-forming galaxies at z=1-7, combining ultra-deep JWST/NIRSpec observations from the MARTA survey with archival spectroscopy. We assemble 244 galaxies with [OIII]4363 detections and derive direct Te-based abundances. New empirical strong-line calibrations for N/O, Ne/O, S/O, and Ar/O extend the analysis to an additional 514 galaxies. We find distinct abundance-metallicity trends. N/O is enhanced by 0.18 dex in median relative to local galaxies, with a stronger enhancement at low metallicity. Direct measurements reveal decreasing S/O and Ar/O with increasing metallicity, while strong-line measurements suggest a flattening at higher metallicities, especially for S/O. We also identify a stellar-mass dependence in the O/Ar-Ar/H plane, with lower-mass galaxies exhibiting lower O/Ar at fixed Ar/H, consistent with differences in star-formation efficiency and delayed SNe Ia enrichment. Ne/O remains approximately constant up to 12+log(O/H)=8.2, with a mild increase at higher metallicities and no significant redshift evolution. C/O tentatively increases with metallicity, broadly following the local relation. Finally, a forward model shows that observational selection affects the abundance ratios differently: it mainly restricts the accessible metallicity range for Ne/O and Ar/O, but preferentially selects galaxies with enhanced N/O at low metallicity, with a weaker effect for S/O. These results provide new constraints on chemical enrichment at high redshift and highlight the importance of accounting for selection effects when interpreting abundance-metallicity trends.

papers.title: Learning Parameters of dRGT Black Holes in Nonlinear Electrodynamics with Neural Network Scenarios
papers.abstract: Using machine learning methods, we present constraining parameter scenarios of AdS black holes in dRGT-like massive gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics. We first approach the photon sphere, the black hole shadow, and the energy emission rate with the help of high performance parallel computations. To corroborate such optical results, we develop a numerical framework to constrain the electric charge and the nonlinear electrodynamic parameter, for certain gravity regimes, via the shadow observations reported by the Even Horizon Telescope collaboration. Employing neural networks, we then examine the parameter regions of the black holes based on their consistency with EHT observations of M87$^*$, SgrA$^*_{\mathrm{VLTI}}$, and SgrA$^*_{\mathrm{Keck}}$, within the $1-\sigma$ and $2-\sigma$ confidence intervals. As a result, we find that the obtained constraints are consistent with the $SgrA^*_{\mathrm{VLTI}}$ empirical data.

papers.title: Impact of cosmic evolution on the gravitational wave spectrum from cosmic strings
papers.abstract: In the standard cosmological paradigm, the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum from a cosmic string network is well defined. However, early-Universe dynamics can significantly alter this relic signal. We systematically investigate how different new physics epochs in the radiation era--including extra relativistic degrees of freedom, early matter domination, intermediate vacuum domination, and kination--modify string network evolution and loop production. We find that a kination era enhances the stochastic GW signal, whereas the other scenarios suppress the signal to varying degrees. We also demonstrate that late-time dynamical dark energy has a negligible impact on the GW spectrum from cosmic strings.

papers.title: Triaxiality of the Milky Way dark matter halo and the microlensing optical depth towards the Large Magellanic Cloud
papers.abstract: The microlensing optical depth towards the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), $\tau_{\rm LMC}$, bounds the compact-object fraction of the Galactic dark matter halo, but is almost always evaluated for a spherical halo. We compute it for triaxial haloes and show that the shape dependence is carried entirely by the projection of the line of sight onto the halo principal axes: for a scale-free halo $\rho\propto R^{-\alpha}$ at fixed local density it factorises exactly as $\tau/\tau_{\rm sph}=S_\odot^{\alpha}\langle S^{-\alpha}\rangle_w$, with $S(\Omega)$ the ellipsoidal shape function. The LMC lies only $0\fdg78$ from perpendicular to the Sun-Galactic Centre line, making it a near-optimal probe of in-plane elongation and a poor probe of vertical flattening. For the halo shapes favoured by \textit{Gaia} we find $\tau_{\rm LMC}/\tau_{\rm sph}=0.95$--$1.15$ at fixed local density, $1.57$ for the Law-Majewski logarithmic potential, and $0.67$--$1.54$ when the major-axis azimuth is left free. For the Einasto halo required by the declining \textit{Gaia} DR3 rotation curve, truncation near $25\kpc$ is offset by the larger local density it implies and $\tau$ falls by only $7$--$15$ per cent; but the median lens distance moves inwards from $13.4$ to $8.5\kpc$, where the logarithmic slope is steep and rising, amplifying the shape sensitivity: the \textit{Gaia} RR~Lyrae enhancement grows from $15$ to $23$ per cent and the orientation-free range widens to $0.62$--$1.62$. The systematic on the inferred MACHO or primordial-black-hole fraction is two-sided, of order $\pm15$ per cent for the measured shapes and a factor $2.6$ under full orientation freedom, exceeding the statistical errors of the EROS-2 and OGLE bounds.

papers.title: Information Problem in Black Holes and Cosmology and Ghosts in Quadratic Gravity
papers.abstract: Black hole information problem is the question about unitarity of the evolution operator during the collapse and evaporation of the black hole. One can ask the same question about unitarity of quantum and inflationary cosmology. In this paper we argue that in both cases, for black holes and for cosmology, the answer is negative and we face non-unitarity. Such a question can not be addressed by using the fixed classical gravitational background since one has to take into account the backreaction. To his end one uses the semi-classical gravity, which includes the expectation value of the energy - momentum tensor operator of the matter fields. One has to renormalize the energy-momentum tensor and one gets an effective action which contains quadratic terms in scalar curvature and Ricci tensor. Such quadratic gravity contains ghosts which in fact lead to violation of unitarity in black holes and cosmology. We discuss the question whether black holes will emit ghosts. One can try to restrict ourselves to the $f(R)$ gravity that seems is a good approximation to the semi-classical gravity and widely used in cosmology. The black hole entropy in $f(R)$ gravity is different from the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy and from entanglement island entropy. The black hole entropy in $R+R^2$ gravity goes to a constant during the evaporation process. This can be interpreted as another indication to the possible non-unitarity in black holes and cosmology

papers.title: Cosmological Constant and Maximum of Entropy for de Sitter Space
papers.abstract: There are at least two cosmological constants calling for explanation. The first one describes the quasi-de Sitter inflation in the early universe, and the second describes the current acceleration of the universe associated with dark energy. An approach to the computation of the inflationary cosmological constant in the early universe is proposed. The tunneling and no-boundary proposals suggest that the ground state of the early universe is the de Sitter space. In this paper it is argued that the radius of the de Sitter space, i.e. the cosmological constant, can be computed using the principle of maximum entropy. The universe emerges from ``nothing" that corresponds to a minimum of entropy. The entropy reaches its maximal value for the 4-dimensional de Sitter space with the inflationary cosmological constant $\Lambda=3\pi\,\exp\{-\psi(3/2)\}$, where $\psi$ is the digamma function, $\Lambda\approx 9.087$ in Planck units.
